text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Portugal Telecom (PT) was valued at 1.5 trillion escudos by a banking consortium formed by Banco Portugues de Investimento and Lehman Brothers. The report was delivered to Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho last Tuesday as part of preparations for the third stage privatisation of PT. Another valuation by a consortium led by Banco Essi values PT at 1.1 trillion escudos. The state is expected to privatise some 26 percent of the capital of PT later this year.

- Retail group Jeronimo Martins is considering expanding its business to Ukraine and expects that in 10 years the country will be politically stable, chairman Alexandre Soares dos Santos told the paper.
- The Socialist government will present its plans to revise the constitution and launch a debate on the state of the nation in September.
- Industrial leaders threaten not to raise workers' wages unless the government introduces a new law of collective negotiations by July 15.

- According to data compiled from the National Statistics Institute, Portugal imported 673.3 tonnes of beef from Britain following the imposition of an EU embargo against British beef exports, the newspaper reported. The Agriculture Minsitry said it was unaware of violations of the embargo.
- Batteries' company Tudor is negotiating the purchase of one or two batteries companies in Brazil, and the deal should be concluded by year-end, its president Joao Salvador told the paper.
- The 1995 budget deficit was undervalued by 158.6 billion escudos, according to an assessment of the Audit Court made available to the newspaper.
